name: Sierra Leone

chips.label: Partial data · 3/5 pillars
chips.why: Scored on the pillars we have data for. Its score is not directly comparable to a fully-measured country - the missing pillars are unmeasured, not zero.

chips.label: Earned prosperity
chips.why: Institutions roughly match or exceed what income predicts - durable.
chips.rule: MI residual vs. the log-GDP regression (the durability gap): below -0.03 → granted, otherwise earned (a ±0.03 tolerance treats near-zero gaps as in-line).

chips.label: Some imbalance · weakest: Institutions
chips.why: Spread between the strongest and weakest pillar - the country's structural shape.

verdict: Mixed structural profile - prosperity matched by institutions.

checks.title: Durability gate
checks.headline: earned-vs-granted +0.07
checks.detail: Institutions match or exceed what the country's income would predict. Prosperity here looks earned, and durable.

checks.title: Weakest link
checks.headline: Institutions is lowest
checks.detail: Institutions is the pillar dragging the score down. A chain breaks at its weakest link, so this is where the structural risk concentrates.

checks.title: Room to rise
checks.headline: low base
checks.detail: Starting from a low institutional base, the country is structurally eligible to climb. This is eligibility, not a forecast - the effect only showed up strongly in the 2000s global growth wave.
